what: The second reading of the red line, session 250 (2026-11-17), after the presentation. The red line joined two readers' rules: the Field's wider "quotes or carries the harmed's own words" (46 first reports from the press) and the Atelier's finer one (30 first reports). The Atelier's critique of 2026-11-15 (ho-2026-11-15-atelier-11) asks that a voice and a telling not look alike. Four convened machine readers, who saw neither the Field's nor the Atelier's codes nor this page, read the first report of all 76 again by the Atelier's stated rule, two readers to each report, on the snapshot's text up to 6,000 characters and, beyond that, every later paragraph holding a quotation mark up to 3,000 more. The Atelier's 30 were mixed in unmarked, as a measure of whether the readers apply its rule as it did; its codes stand for its 30. Where the two readers of one of the Field's 46 differed, the conductor read the report a third time.

rule.own: the first report carries, in direct quotation or as reproduced writing, words of a natural person the column names as harmed (by name, or as a member of a group it names), which that person gave to the reporter or to the public themselves; or that person wrote the report
rule.body: the party the column names is an organisation, and its statement or its spokesperson is quoted directly
rule.other: the harmed's words or position reach the report only in paraphrase, or through someone else: a lawyer, counsel in court, kin after a death, an official, a campaign, an association, a complaint summarised
rule.none: no word of the harmed, direct or relayed

drawn.voice: own or body: a red line through the first word
